character: The QS: the same narrator as 'Six bids. Six formats.' A mid-career quantity surveyor (late 30s to 40s) with a general, urban professional New Zealand accent (Auckland or Wellington office), not broad or rural and not Australian. This time he chaired the meeting: he wrote 'Chase painter' in the minutes six weeks running, and he's quietly owning it. Calm, dry and deadpan, amused at himself rather than annoyed at anyone, firmly on the painter's side. He is a fictional narrator: he never claims to be a QSME customer and never speaks as the founder. Voice Design fallback, for when no library voice passes the casting line: "New Zealander around 40, general NZ accent, urban and professional, not broad, low-mid register, dry and unhurried, slightly sheepish but amused, close-mic phone recording in a quiet site office, conversational, not a narrator or announcer."
casting_line: Six weeks we've chased the painter. Turns out it was the switchboard. Yeah, nah. We owe him a coffee.
continuous_read_v2:
Six weeks we've chased the painter.

Painter's starting a week late. Finish didn't move.

Something else moved it. Nobody minuted that.

Purple decides your finish date.

Our painter? Grey.

Grey has room to move.

Finish didn't budge.

Purple slips a day...

...the finish slips a day.

Q-S-me calls it "What drives the finish date".

You can call it the critical path.

We owe the painter a coffee.

Book a thirty-minute demo at Q-S-me dot build.

lines.text_v2: Six weeks we've chased the painter.
lines.text_v3: [sighs] Six weeks we've chased the painter.
lines.delivery: Flat, tired, a man reading his own minutes back. Light lean on 'six', falling end on 'painter', no lift. Out by 2.6 so the pen scratch on the sixth underline (2.12 to 2.6) and the '(Again.)' jolt at 2.7 land in near-silence.

lines.on_screen: Painter: starting a week late. (3.25) / Finish date: didn't move. (4.35) over the 'actions carried forward' ledger, weeks 9 to 12 tinting green while weeks 13 and 14 are still greyed
lines.text_v2: Painter's starting a week late. Finish didn't move.
lines.text_v3: Painter's starting a week late. Finish didn't move.
lines.delivery: Two plain facts with a real beat between them (0.3 to 0.4 s). 'Painter's starting a week late' ends level; 'Finish didn't move' starts as the second caption lands (about 4.4) and drops on 'move', a little puzzled. Out by 6.4.

lines.on_screen: Something else moved it. (6.75) / Nobody minuted that. (7.95) as weeks 13 and 14 tick out to Thu 26 Nov (6.6 to 7.55) and the '+9 working days' sticker slams on at 7.6
lines.text_v2: Something else moved it. Nobody minuted that.
lines.text_v3: Something else moved it. [pause] Nobody minuted that.
lines.delivery: 'Something else moved it' quiet and matter-of-fact, finished by about 7.55 so the sticker slam (7.6) lands clear. Then 'Nobody minuted that' at about 7.95, slower, the self-own starting to dawn. Out by 9.25, before the swipe at 9.45.

lines.on_screen: Purple decides your finish date. (12.0) as the chain rings in purple (11.85 to 12.67), after the pill (9.7 to 11.9) and the tick at 11.4
lines.delivery: Plain and even, like reading the key on the chart. Light lean on 'Purple'. No sell. Out by 13.7.

lines.on_screen: Our painter? Grey. (13.65) as the biro circles the Painting bar (13.71 to 14.13); the note 'nobody minuted this' sits on the switchboard
lines.delivery: A small question, then a flat, slightly sheepish 'Grey.' Let 'Grey' fall. Out by 15.05.

lines.on_screen: Grey has room to move. (15.3) as the cursor grabs Painting (15.71) and drags it a week right (15.8 to 16.55); the 9:16 pushes in gently from 15.22
lines.delivery: Unhurried, a demonstrator's calm. Read it while the bar is moving. Out by 17.05.

lines.on_screen: Sticky notes 'Painter: 1 week late' (16.63) and 'didn't move ✓' beside 'Finish: Thu 26 Nov' (16.85); toast '1 moved · Undo' (16.69)
lines.delivery: Dry and pleased with the proof, a half-smile at most. Falling end. Out by 18.3.

lines.on_screen: Purple slips a day, (18.75) during the push-in on the chart (18.67 to 19.15); the cursor heads for Electrical fit-off
lines.delivery: Set-up half of one sentence: level, open-ended, a slight hang on 'day'. Out by 20.1, so the drag (19.55 to 19.87) carries its own sound under the tail.

lines.on_screen: the finish slips a day. (on screen since 19.5); the finish note flips Thu 26 Nov → Fri 27 Nov at 20.25, '+1 day' note, toast '1 moved — 3 that follow it came too · Undo' (20.05)
lines.delivery: Pick-up of vo08, landing 'finish' right on the date flip at 20.25. Flat and certain, a touch heavier than vo08. Out by 21.9.

lines.on_screen: The A4 'Construction programme' slides onto the desk (22.1 to 22.6) and the camera zooms onto the purple-ring sentence (22.72 to 23.3); caption 'QSME calls it “What drives the finish date”.' from 23.3; the highlighter runs 23.45 to 23.9
lines.text_v2: Q-S-me calls it "What drives the finish date".
lines.text_v3: Q-S-me calls it "What drives the finish date".
lines.delivery: Light and practical, like handing it across the table. The feature name is said plainly, as a label, not sold: a tiny lift on 'What drives', falling on 'finish date'. It now matches the caption word for word, so sound-on viewers hear the product's own label. Out by 25.8.

lines.on_screen: You can call it the critical path. (25.8) over the zoomed, highlighted line 'Any one of them running late moves the whole finish.'
lines.text_v2: You can call it the critical path.
lines.text_v3: You can call it the critical path.
lines.delivery: A dry aside between professionals, a small shrug in the voice. No emphasis on 'critical path', no jargon pride. Starts with the caption. Out by 28.15 (it may tail into the zoom-out).

lines.on_screen: We owe the painter a coffee. (28.1, held to 30.75); a takeaway cup with PAINTER on the sleeve lands beside the printout 27.9 to 28.3
lines.text_v2: We owe the painter a coffee.
lines.text_v3: [chuckles softly] We owe the painter a coffee.
lines.delivery: The self-own. Warm and sheepish, the joke on us, never on him. Tiny lean on 'coffee'. Let the cup set-down sound sit just before the line. Out by 30.5.

lines.on_screen: End card: QSME logo / Chase the right delay. / Book a 30-minute demo / qsme.build
lines.text_v2: Book a thirty-minute demo at Q-S-me dot build.
lines.text_v3: Book a thirty-minute demo at Q-S-me dot build.
lines.delivery: Same voice, same calm, no announcer lift. 'Q-S-me' is kyoo-ess-mee, never 'kiss me' and never four letters. Falling end on 'build'. Starts as the logo lands (30.9). Out by 33.7.

post_processing: Time base: every time is seconds on outputs/chase-the-painter-4x5.mp4 (33.8 s, retimed 2026-10-04). outputs/chase-the-painter-9x16.mp4 runs on exactly the same clock, so one VO/SFX/music stem fits both with tools/mux.

Generation (v2 default): render continuous_read_v2 three times on the chosen voice (blank lines are the pauses), then slice it and place each line at its start_s. Regenerate any line that overruns max_s rather than speeding it up past 1.05x. vo08 and vo09 must come from the same take so the sentence carries across the drag.

Silence is on purpose: 2.6 to 3.3 (pen and '(Again.)'), 9.25 to 12.05 (swipe, View, the cursor resting on the checkbox, the tick at 11.4, the rings drawing on), 18.3 to 18.8 (push-in), 21.85 to 23.35 (desk cut, paper slide, zoom), 30.5 to 30.9 (end card in).

SFX (royalty-free or ElevenLabs SFX after the upgrade): page flicks on each scroll (0.3, 0.62, 0.94, 1.26, 1.58), pen click 1.86, biro scratch 2.12 to 2.6, soft swipe 2.92 and 9.45, ticking digits 6.6 to 7.55, sticker slap 7.6, UI click on View 10.2, soft tick on the checkbox 11.4, light ring 'pops' 11.85 to 12.51, biro scribble 12.9 to 13.73 and 13.71 to 14.13, low drag whoosh 15.8 and 19.55, soft thunk on drop 16.55 and 19.87, one muted 'tock' on the finish flip 20.25, paper slide 22.1, highlighter squeak 23.45 to 23.9 (under vo10, keep it low), cup set-down 28.3. Duck all SFX 10 to 12 dB under VO.
Music: see post.md (Music). Bed at -24 LUFS under VO, -18 when VO is silent; near-silence for the tick at 11.4; resolve on the end card at 30.75.
Pronunciation: Q-S-me = kyoo-ess-mee. qsme.build = 'Q-S-me dot build'. 'Fit-off' as one word stress on 'fit'.
If an AI voice ships, switch on the platform AI-content labels (LinkedIn and YouTube 'altered or synthetic content'), because the narrator is a synthetic voice playing a fictional QS.
